question:
**The given sentence is divided into three segments. Select the option that has the segment with a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'no error' as your answer.**

I miss you / when you move / to another building.
solution:
The erroneous part of the sentence is:** I miss you**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The error is in the verb tense.
 
• The correct tense should be future tense, "**I will miss you**," since the action of missing will happen in the future when the person moves to another building.
 
• The original sentence is in the present tense, "**I miss you**," which indicates an ongoing or habitual action.
 
• However, since the action of missing will occur in the future when the person moves to another building, the correct tense to use is the future tense.
 
• By changing "**I miss you**" to "**I will miss you**," the sentence accurately reflects that the speaker's feeling of missing the person will take place in the future. This maintains proper tense consistency in the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is** option 3**.

**Corrected sentence:** *I will miss you when you move to another building. *
